title: How do we draw a shape with all four sides equal?
description: A side and a fifty degree angle are drawn first, and two arcs of the same length find the last corner. Keeko doubts that a shape with four equal sides must be a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: the last corner is the point that is five centimetres from both B and D, so two arcs fix it. Watch for students who think four equal sides force right angles at every corner.

source: Construct a quadrilateral ABCD with all sides 5 cm and ∠A = 50°.
video_script.why: The child sees that a compass arc of the side length finds the corner that is the same distance from two points, so all four sides come out equal.
video_script.substitution: the book's own construction with a 50 degree angle and equal sides of 5 cm
video_script.anchor: the shape ABCD built from the book's side AB, the 50 degree angle at A and two equal arcs
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a shape with all four sides equal must be a square, but the angle at A is 50 degrees, not 90.
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh B C D is a rhombus

final_answer.value: ABCD is a rhombus with a 50° angle, and it is not a square
final_answer.spoken: a rhombus with a fifty degree angle that is not a square

maths_rules: AB = AD = 5 cm, with angle DAB = 50 degrees
C is 5 cm from B and 5 cm from D, so BC = DC = 5 cm
AB = BC = CD = DA = 5 cm, so ABCD is a rhombus
angle A = 50 degrees, not 90 degrees, so ABCD is not a square
video_script.design: One idea: two equal arcs find the last corner. One figure, built a step at a time, stays on the board through the idea part.
open_questions: The side length five centimetres comes from the worklist; the book text does not give a length for this construction.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it must be a square, because all four sides are equal.

<bookmark mark='kind'/>Four equal sides make a rhombus, and a square is the special one with ninety degrees.
